In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

.

Surah Al-Mutaffifin

It is Medinan.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: It is the first surah to be revealed in Medina. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Medina, its people were the worst of people in measuring and weighing, so Allah the Exalted revealed this surah, and they became upright; they are the most complete of people in measuring and weighing up to (this) day.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Woe to the defrauders﴾. Al-wayl (woe): it is an invocation of severity and destruction.

It is related from al-Suddi that it is a valley in Hell, in which the pus of the people of the Fire flows.

His saying: ﴿to the defrauders﴾ are those who do not give full measure and weight, and who diminish.

Al-Zajjaj said: He was named mutaffif because he does not cheat by this act with a slight thing (al-tatfif), that is, a small amount. We have already explained that it was revealed concerning the people of Medina. It was also said: it was revealed concerning Abu Juhayna, a man from Medina who had two saas, and he would measure with one of them against the people, that is, from the people, and it is said: "iktala ʿala fulan," meaning: I took my full due from so-and-so.

His saying: ﴿who take full measure﴾, that is, they take their rights in full, and it is said: they take it in excess.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 83, verse 3:**

And His saying: ﴿When they measure out to them﴾ means: they measure out for them.

Likewise: ﴿or weigh out to them﴾, i.e., they weigh out for them.

[This] was said by Abu 'Ubayda, al-Akhfash and al-Farra'. Al-Akhfash is Sa'id ibn Mas'ada, and he is al-Akhfash al-Kabir (the Elder). Al-Farra' said: it is a Hijazi dialect (lughah hijaziyya). I heard some of them in Makkah say: "Idha sadara al-nas, atayna al-tajir, fa-kala al-madda wa-l-madayn ila al-'am al-muqbil," meaning: he measured for us.

And ﴿they cause loss﴾ means: they diminish [the measure].

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 83, verse 4:

And His saying: ﴿Do they not think that they will be resurrected?﴾ That is: Do those not become certain that they will be resurrected?

It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: Five for five. No people broke the covenant except that Allah gave their enemy power over them. No people judged by other than what Allah has sent down except that poverty spread among them. Immorality did not appear among a people except that death spread among them. They did not diminish the measure and the balance except that they were prevented from vegetation and afflicted with years of drought. No people withheld the zakat except that rain was withheld from them.

It is related from Malik ibn Dinar, who said: I entered upon a neighbour of mine to visit him when death had come upon him, and I began to prompt him with the words of the testimony of faith, while he was saying: Two mountains of fire, two mountains of fire.

He kept saying it until he died. I inquired about him, and they said: He had a measure and a balance with which he would cheat.

It has also been said regarding His saying: ﴿Do they not think﴾, meaning: that they do not act as one who thinks that they will be resurrected.

And His saying: ﴿For a Great Day﴾ is the Day of Resurrection.

He named it "great" because of the greatness of what happens in it and its severity.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 83, verse 6:

And His saying: ﴿On the day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾. Ibn 'Umar narrated from the Prophet that he said: "They will stand for a hundred years upon the heads of their graves." And from some of the Companions: three hundred years. And from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As: they will stand for a thousand years in darkness.

Hammad ibn Salamah narrated from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet that he said concerning the Most High's saying ﴿On the day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾: he said: "They will stand until the sweat reaches the tips of their ears."

He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Abu'l-Husayn ibn al-Naqur informed us of this hadith, saying: Abu Tahir al-Mukhallis informed us.

Ibn Bint Mani' – that is Abu'l-Qasim al-Baghawi – informed us: Abu Nasr al-Tammar informed us: Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, the hadith.

Muslim recorded it in his Sahih from Abu Nasr al-Tammar. Al-Bukhari also mentioned this hadith with its chain, and he mentioned that they will stand until the sweat reaches the middle of their ears.

Sulaym ibn 'Amir narrated from al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The sun will be brought near to the heads of the creation, until it is at the distance of a mil from their heads." Sulaym said: I do not know whether he meant the mil of distance or the mil of the kohl-stick. He said: "The sun will scorch them, and they will be in sweat according to their deeds. Among them is one whom the sweat reaches to his ankles, and among them one whom it reaches to his knees, and among them one whom it reaches to his waist, and among them one whom it bridles completely." And the Messenger of Allah placed his hand on (his) mouth.

And in some reports: "The sweat will go down into the earth seventy cubits." And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 83, verse 7:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Nay, indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin﴾. "Nay" (kalla) is a word of restraint, reproach and warning, as if He is saying: "The matter is not as you suppose, so desist."

And His words: ﴿Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin﴾ have two interpretations. The first: it is the record of deeds. The second: it is the spirits of the disbelievers. The first is the more apparent.

And His words: ﴿in Sijjin﴾: it is a form (fa'il) derived from prison (sijn). 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: it is the lowest earth, in which Iblis and his offspring are.

It is related from Mujahid: it is a rock beneath the seventh earth, which is turned over, and beneath it is placed the record of the wicked.

It is related from the rabbi (al-Hibr) that he said regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin﴾: it is the spirit of the disbeliever, which is seized and ascends with it to the heaven, and the heaven refuses to receive it. Then it descends with it to the earth, and the earth refuses to receive it. So it descends with it beneath the earths, and it is placed beneath the cheek of Iblis.

And in some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed, al-Falaq is a well in Hell, covered, and Sijjin is a well in Hell, open."
And His saying: ﴿And what will make you know what Sijjin is?﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: The Messenger of God did not know it until God informed him of it.
"And His saying: ﴿A written record﴾, i.e., the record of the wicked. Some of them said: "A written record" refers back to Sijjin, and the more correct view is what we have explained."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 83, verse 10:

His saying: ﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾. We have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 83, verses 11–13:

And His saying: ﴿Those who deny the Day of Judgment, and none denies it except every transgressor, sinful, when Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Tales of the ancients."﴾ That is: the fabrications (abatil) of the ancients and their lies.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 83, verses 11–13:

And His saying: ﴿Those who deny the Day of Judgment, and none denies it except every transgressor, sinful, when Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Tales of the ancients."﴾ That is: the fabrications (abatil) of the ancients and their lies.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 83, verses 11–13:

And His saying: ﴿Those who deny the Day of Judgment, and none denies it except every transgressor, sinful, when Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Tales of the ancients."﴾ That is: the fabrications (abatil) of the ancients and their lies.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 83, verse 14:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Nay! Rather, what they have been earning has covered over their hearts.﴾ That is: it overcame their hearts.

Al-Farra' said: They multiplied their sins and transgressions, so they encompassed their hearts.

Al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim narrated from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "When the servant commits a sin, a black spot is marked on his heart. If he gives it up, seeks forgiveness and repents, it is polished clean. But if he returns to it, more is added to it until his heart is sealed. That is the 'ran' (covering) of which Allah the Most High said: ﴿Nay! Rather, what they have been earning has covered over their hearts.﴾"

He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: This noble hadith was related to us by Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Zaynabi, who said: Abu Tahir al-Mukhlis related to us, who said: al-Baghawi related to us, who said: Zaghba related to us, from al-Layth, from Ibn 'Ajlan, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim, the hadith.

It is said: "ran" means he covered over and veiled, and this is close to the first meaning.

Al-Hasan said: It is sin upon sin until his heart becomes black. A similar report was transmitted from Mujahid.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 83, verse 15:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nay, indeed they, on that Day, will be veiled from their Lord.﴾ In the verse there is evidence that the believers will see Allah, exalted is He. This evidence has been transmitted from Malik and al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on them both. Malik said: When Allah veiled the wicked from seeing Him, it indicates that He will manifest Himself to the believers so that they see Him.

The like of this was narrated by al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman from al-Shafi'i. Al-Rabi' said: I said to al-Shafi'i: Will Allah be seen by this? He said: Had I not been certain that Allah is seen in Paradise, I would not have worshipped Him in this world.

This evidence has also been narrated from Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Tha'lab al-Shaybani, Ibn 'Abbas.

And from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: Were the believers to know that they will not see Allah in the Hereafter, their souls would depart in this world.

In the verse there is clearer evidence in meaning for what we have said, because He mentioned His saying: ﴿Nay, indeed they, on that Day, will be veiled from their Lord﴾ concerning the disbelievers as a punishment for them. So if we said that the believers are veiled, it would not be valid to make it a punishment for the disbelievers.

Al-Kalbi mentioned in his exegesis, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this verse, that the believers will see Him in Paradise, and the disbelievers will be veiled.

And from al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl, who said: Just as He veiled them in this world from His oneness, so likewise in the Hereafter He veils them from seeing Him.
Wa-qawluhu: ﴿Then indeed they will surely burn in the Blazing Fire﴾, meaning: they will indeed enter the Blazing Fire.
And His saying: ﴿Then it will be said, "This is what you used to deny."﴾ It is said to them in the manner of reproach and rebuke.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 83, verse 18:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyūn.﴾ Al-Farrāʾ said: it means elevation upon elevation (irtifāʿ baʿd irtifāʿ).

Kaʿb (al-Aḥbār) said: The soul of the believer is seized and taken up to the heaven, and the angels receive it until it reaches the seventh heaven, and it is placed beneath the Throne.

It is said: the Book here is the Book of Deeds. We have already explained that this is the more apparent of the two views. The meaning is that it is placed in the highest of places, to make manifest the baseness of the deeds of the wicked.
And His saying: ﴿And what will make you know what ʿIlliyyūn is?﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: He did not know until Allah informed him.

Its words, "A written record, witnessed by those brought near" (﴿Kitabun marqum yashhaduhu al-muqarrabun﴾): meaning, a written book, or a book upon which is a mark of acceptance; the angels witness it. It was said: those brought near of every heaven witness it.

Its words, "A written record, witnessed by those brought near" (﴿Kitabun marqum yashhaduhu al-muqarrabun﴾): meaning, a written book, or a book upon which is a mark of acceptance; the angels witness it. It was said: those brought near of every heaven witness it.
Allah's saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in pleasure﴾, meaning: in the pleasure of Paradise.

On the words of Allah: ﴿Upon the couches, they will look on﴾. "Al-arā'ik" is the plural of "arīka," and it refers to the couches (ࣰsurar) inside the canopied enclosures (al-ḥijāl), as we have explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 83, verse 24:

And His saying: ﴿You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss﴾, meaning: the brightness and beauty of bliss (al-Naʿīm).

And this is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾.

And His saying: ﴿They will be given to drink of a sealed wine﴾ (yusqawna min raheeqin makhtum). Masruq narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, that both of them said: "The raheeq (a pure, refined drink) is the khamr (wine)." It was also said: "It is the drink in which there is no adulteration."

And His saying: ﴿sealed﴾ means: no hands have touched it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 83, verse 26:

And His saying: ﴿Its seal is musk﴾. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: its end is the scent of musk, and its taste is the taste of the most delicious of drinks.

And it is related from a group of the exegetes that they said: when one reaches the end of the drink, one finds the scent of musk. The meaning is that the drink which exists in this world has, at its end, turbidity and what the soul dislikes, so Allah the Exalted mentioned that the drink of the Hereafter is contrary to that.

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) read "khatimah misk" [with a fatha on the ta' and the ta' marbuta], and Isa ibn Umar read "khatimatu misk" [with a kasra on the ta'], and it has been said regarding the meaning of His saying, "khatamahu misk" [with a fatha on the ta']: that its clay (tinatuhu) is musk; and regarding His saying, "khatimahu misk" [with a kasra on the ta']: that its end and its outcome is musk.

And His saying: ﴿And for that let the competitors compete﴾, meaning: let those who hasten hasten [to it]. Al-munafasah (competition) is the manifestation of intense seeking, and it has been said: it is the racing to attain it.

And His saying: ﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn 'Abbas, and 'Alqamah from Ibn Mas'ud, that it is the most noble drink of the people of Paradise: the ones brought near (al-muqarrabun) drink it pure, and it is mixed for the righteous (al-abrar). Mansur related the like of this from Malik ibn al-Harith.

It was also said concerning Tasnim: it is a spring that flows down (tatassamu) upon the people of Paradise from the lofty chambers (al-ghuraf). And it was said: it is a spring of water.

His saying: ﴿A spring from which those brought near drink﴾. We have already explained it. The accusative of "عينا" (in the sense of the grammatical accusative, *naṣb*) is according to the meaning: "I mean a spring," or "I intend a spring."

.

His saying: "بها" means "منها," that is, "from it."

Almighty God's words: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes﴾ are the disbelievers.

It was also said: this refers to specific people among the Quraysh, among them Abu Jahl, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, and others.

And His words: ﴿used to laugh at those who believed﴾. It was said: this refers to specific people among the believers, among them Khabbab, Bilal, Abu Dharr, Ammar, and others from the poor Companions.
And His saying: ﴿And when they passed by them, they winked at one another.﴾ That is: they gestured with their eyes and their eyebrows.

And His saying: ﴿And when they returned to their own people, they returned jesting [fākihīn]﴾, meaning: exulting (mu'jabīn) in their own deeds.

It was also said: happy of heart, rejoicing (mustabshirīn).

The Arabs say: a man is fakih and fākih when he is one who laughs much and is good-natured.
And His saying: ﴿When they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are surely misguided."﴾ That is: they strayed from the truth and the path of right guidance, and followed falsehood.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 83, verse 33:

And His saying: ﴿But they were not sent as guardians over them.﴾ That is, they were not sent over them to watch over their deeds.

That is, the disbelievers were not sent over the believers. The meaning is: they were not appointed over the believers to watch over them regarding what they do.

It is said: this verse was revealed concerning the hypocrites.

It is said: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl and his companions.

And His saying: ﴿from those who believed﴾ refers to ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, and his companions.

And this is a distant opinion.

And His saying: ﴿So today those who believed﴾ are the believers from among the Companions of the Messenger.

.

And His saying: ﴿from the disbelievers they laugh at, reclining on couches, gazing﴾. In some exegeses it is said that Paradise has openings (kuwa) toward the people of the Fire; whenever the people of Paradise wish, they open the openings, look down at the Fire, and laugh at them.

We have already explained the meaning of al-arai'k (couches) earlier.

And His saying: ﴿So today those who believed﴾ are the believers from among the Companions of the Messenger.

.

And His saying: ﴿from the disbelievers they laugh at, reclining on couches, gazing﴾. In some exegeses it is said that Paradise has openings (kuwa) toward the people of the Fire; whenever the people of Paradise wish, they open the openings, look down at the Fire, and laugh at them.

We have already explained the meaning of al-arai'k (couches) earlier.
And His saying: ﴿Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ That is, have the disbelievers been recompensed for what they used to do? That is, for what they used to do.
